chapter: Billy Pierce Studio and New York tap
title: Nazarro discovers them; black dancers who used the studio
summary: Buck and Nat Nazarro find them in the third week; Green lists Louis Brown, Johnny Dillman, Buster Newman and Stretch Johnson among the few black dancers there.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So in after only nine days, did you
Yeah, by -- about in the third week. Mr. Buck -- just Buck -- Nat Nazarra and Buck -- one of the Buck'in Bubbles.
He discovered you, or was Nat Nazarra with him?
They just came into the place they usually would come in to see if they could find some new talent?
Now, who else was there at the same time? Was anybody else that was well known other than Eleanor Powell coming in? Any other black dancers? How about Henry Le_______?

Yeah, well, there was a fellow, the twins' brother, he was Louis Brown. He used to come down there and practice. And there was a fellow named Johnny Dillman. He's a great musician now. He's a trumpet player. He plays trumpet. But he was a dancer at that time, you know. He's a dance teacher rather. He was the one that was up on the second floor in the Billy Pierce Studio, you know.

Wouldn't you say it wasn't that many black performers going in and out the Billy Pierce Studios? It was just mostly the people that worked as assistants or playing the piano? Billy Pierce himself was a very strict man because of white performers, you know, lots of white showgirls and that. He was very strict. The school was run very strictly.

That's right. That's right. There was another colored gent that came in there named Buster Newman. See, he turned out to be a dance teacher, see. But like I say, the twins' brother, Louis Brown, he was about the only other Negro that was in there. He wasn't taking lessons. He was teaching himself. He was practicing there, you see.

Oh, yeah, and there was another gent too, Stretch Johnson. He was -- they were of these famous Cotton Club boys, you know, and that was a popular club in New York City, but it was up in Harlem, see. And they used to come there and practice.
Of course, Billy was also -- excuse me -- always looking for people that could teach. See, ever since he found Buddy, he would always be looking for more Buddy Bradleys, you know.
So that's maybe what he had in mind with you.
